title: Separated locally quasi-finite algebraic spaces over schemes are schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T$ be a scheme over $S$, let $E$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:E\to T$ be a morphism. Assume that $f$ is locally quasi-finite in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale morphism $V\to E$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Assume also that the diagonal $E\to E\times_T E$ is a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then there exist a scheme $Z$ over $T$ and an isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $T$ between $h_Z$ and $E$.

proof.text: Regard $E$ as an algebraic space over $T$. Indeed its fppf sheaf is the sheaf of sections of $E$ with the specified composite to $T$; the sheaf condition restricts to that fibre. Its relative diagonal is a base change of its diagonal over $S$, and its original atlas, equipped with the composite map to $T$, is still representable surjective etale [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lem-a1-space-affine-atlas-open-cover] over $T$. It gives open subspaces $E_i$ covering $E$, affine opens $T_i\subseteq T$ through which $E_i$ maps, and affine schemes $U_i$ with representable surjective etale maps $U_i\to E_i$. It is enough to prove each $E_i$ is a scheme by [lem-pc-schemes-criterion]: the fppf sheaf is a Zariski sheaf, the inclusions are representable open immersions, and the pullbacks of this open covering along any scheme section cover that scheme. These are precisely its three hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 03XX, first two proof paragraphs; Properties of Spaces Tags 03FY and 03JH.

proof.text: Each $E_i\to T_i$ satisfies the hypotheses of the item. For a representable etale scheme chart $V\to E_i$, the composite $V\to E_i\to E$ is again representable etale: an open immersion is etale and etale composites are etale on scheme tests [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite by hypothesis; apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change] along $T_i\to T$. The source of this base change is $V\times_TT_i=V$, since $V\to T$ factors through the open $T_i$, so $V\to T_i$ is locally quasi-finite. The relative diagonal of $E_i/T_i$ is the pullback of that of $E/T$ to $E_i\times_T E_i$: the fibre products over $T_i$ and $T$ agree because $T_i\to T$ is a monomorphism. Its scheme tests are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. We henceforth write $X\to T$ and $U\to X$ for one such piece; both $T$ and $U$ are affine.

source.place: Tag 03XX, first two proof paragraphs: the hypotheses persist on the chosen open pieces.

proof.text: Put $R=U\times_XU$. The diagonal representability in [def-trf-algebraic-space] makes this a scheme. Its projections $s,t:R\to U$ are etale and surjective by base change of the atlas [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By the fibre-product universal property it is an equivalence relation, and the map $j:R\to U\times_TU$ is the scheme base change of $\Delta_{X/T}$; it is a closed immersion by the assumed testwise closedness. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes $U\times_TU$ affine. The affine criterion for a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore makes $R$ affine. Finally $U\to T$ is locally quasi-finite by the chartwise hypothesis applied to $U\to X$.

source.place: Tag 03XX, third proof paragraph: affine etale relation R=U times_X U.

proof.text: The fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$ is $X$. To verify this identification, a section $x\in X(H)$ lifts on the covering $H\times_XU\to H$, which is a surjective etale morphism of schemes by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Such a morphism is an fppf covering since etale means flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fppf-site]. Two lifts have the same image exactly when they are related by $R(H)=U(H)\times_{X(H)}U(H)$. These local bijections glue by the sheaf axiom, giving $U/R\simeq X$. The same verification applies after any base change to a scheme over $T$, since the atlas remains etale surjective [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The quotient and its universal property are the ones in [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient].

source.place: Tag 03XX, third proof paragraph, using Spaces Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation); the quotient identification is written out.

proof.text: Fix a point $x\in|X|$ and choose $u\in U$ mapping to it, using surjectivity of the atlas. All hypotheses of [lem-a1-proper-etale-relation-finite-neighbourhood] hold by step 3: $U,R,T$ are affine, $U/T$ is locally quasi-finite, the relation map is closed, and $s,t$ are etale. Obtain an affine etale neighbourhood $(T',p')\to(T,p)$, a point $u'$ over $u$, and clopen pieces $U',R'$ finite over $T'$ such that $R'$ is the full restricted relation on $U'\subset U\times_TT'$. Its projections $s',t'$ are etale. Here $p$ is the image of $u$ in $T$; no finiteness of the entire atlas or of $X/T$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 03XX, fourth proof paragraph, invoking More on Groupoids Tag 03X5.

proof.text: The finite morphisms $U',R'\to T'$ have affine sources because $T'$ is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Write their coordinate rings as $A',B'$ over $D=\Gamma(T',\mathcal O_{T'})$. The finite set generating $B'$ as a $D$-module also generates it as an $A'$-module via either projection, since $D\to B'$ factors through either map $A'\to B'$. Thus $s',t'$ are finite. They are etale by step 5, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. They are therefore finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Apply [lem-a1-finite-flat-affine-relation-quotient] over $T'$: the quotient $Q=U'/R'$ is an affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 03XX, fourth proof paragraph, invoking Groupoids Tag 03BM; the finiteness of the projections is checked in coordinates.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens], the inclusion $U'\to U\times_TT'$ induces an open immersion $Q\to (U\times_TT')/(R\times_TT')$. Its hypotheses hold: the original projections after base change are etale and surjective by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], so they are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]; the clopen inclusion of $U'$ is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], hence flat and locally of finite presentation as well; and the relation on $U'$ is the full restricted relation from step 5. By step 4 the target quotient is $X_{T'}$. Thus the affine scheme $Q$ represents an open subspace $V'\subset X_{T'}$. Its point coming from $u'$ maps to $x$.

source.place: Tag 03XX, fourth proof paragraph, invoking Spaces Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens).

proof.text: The map $V'\to T'$ is a morphism between affine schemes; its inverse images of principal affine opens are spectra of localizations of its coordinate ring, so it is affine, and in particular quasi-affine (factor it as its identity open immersion followed by this affine map). Apply [lem-a1-etale-quasi-affine-image-scheme] to $X\to T$, the affine etale map $T'\to T$, and $V'$. It supplies a representable open subspace $W\subseteq X$ whose underlying open set is the image of $|V'|$. In particular $x\in W$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, representable opens cover $X$, and [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] makes $X$ representable: it is a Zariski sheaf and, for each section over a scheme $H$, the base changes of these representable opens are open subschemes covering $H$, so the required functor covering condition holds. Apply this to every $E_i$ from step 1 and use the same criterion once more to obtain a scheme $Z$ representing $E$. For the composite natural transformation $\alpha:h_Z\simeq E\to h_T$, define $g=\alpha_Z(\mathrm{id}_Z):Z\to T$. Naturality gives $\alpha_H(a)=g\circ a$ for every $a:H\to Z$, so the representing isomorphism is over $T$, as required.

source.place: Tag 03XX, final proof paragraph, invoking Tag 03XW (lemma-neighbourhood-scheme) and Schemes Tag 01JJ, the gluing criterion used in the proof of Properties of Spaces Tag 03JH.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), entire proof, following its 03FY, 03JH, 03X5, 02WU, 03BM, 03XW route.

lean.statement: theorem exists_scheme_of_separated_locally_quasi_finite {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : Over S) (E : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : E.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hqf : ∀ (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ E.obj.obj), IsEtale a → Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ f)).left) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal f)) : ∃ (Z : Over S) (g : Z ⟶ T) (e : yoneda.obj Z ≅ E.obj.obj), e.hom ≫ f = yoneda.map g
